48094.note: Fish-camp-style seafood restaurant on the Intracoastal Waterway in Palm Valley, sister to Julington Creek Fish Camp.

48154.note: Cuban eatery and bakery south of St. Augustine Beach with roast pork, Cuban coffee and pastelitos.

48173.note: Cash-only Anastasia Island seafood house known for fried shrimp with its house datil pepper sauce and homemade Minorcan clam chowder.
48173.fn: The restaurant's own site says it opened in 1965.

48241.note: Downtown seafood restaurant cooking Florida-caught fish whose spicy red Minorcan chowder of clams, fish and bacon is seasoned with datil pepper.

48269.note: Old riverbank seafood spot under live oaks on the Tolomato River with a floating dock for boaters and outdoor decks.
48269.fn: The restaurant says it is "continuing over 100 years" of serving local seafood; no specific year confirmed.

48312.note: Vilano Beach restaurant on the Intracoastal with a Sunset Oyster Bar, big outdoor deck and dock.

48318.note: Colombian and South American kitchen inside the Ponce Saint Augustine Hotel on US 1.

48349.note: Modern fish-camp-style restaurant on the San Sebastian River docks, sister to Palm Valley and Julington Creek Fish Camps.

48401.note: Fast-casual seafood counter on St. George Street with raw oysters, two chowders and fried shrimp baskets.

48410.note: St. Augustine branch of the Gonzmart family's Spanish-Cuban restaurant, with tiled dining rooms and fountains on St. George Street.
48410.fn: The family's 1905 founding belongs to the original Ybor City restaurant in Tampa; this St. Augustine location opened much later.

48413.note: Downtown Cuban café and bakery with a patio, serving sandwiches, empanadas, flan and Cuban coffee daily.
